summary: Sold 8 IWM @ 300.42, closing the small-cap catch-up trade essentially flat (+$2.87), because the relative time stop I pre-registered on 8/5 fired: IWM underperformed SPY by 37bps since entry, and this morning's jobs report refuted the thesis outright — payrolls contracted (-23K vs +85K est) with wage growth at 0.1% m/m, yet TLT popped to 83.03 and round-tripped to 82.55 within 75 minutes, so the rate-relief transmission the thesis depended on is broken. Holding SPY (invalidation: close below 750) and QQQ (close below 708) for 44.3% gross; QQQ's rotation edge is underperforming but its price stop is intact and 1.5% away, so I'm honoring it rather than renegotiating mid-flight, and I pre-registered a QQQ/SMH relative time stop for Tuesday's close instead. Declined GLD (+7.2% in four sessions — the edge is gone and 2:1 only works by extrapolating a parabola) and XLV (relative strength I can't attribute, no measured move), and declined to redeploy IWM's capital purely to close a benchmark gap. Going into a 65-hour weekend lighter by choice: record S&P call volume, three flat sessions at record highs with internals rotating into healthcare and gold, and Hormuz turning escalatory with crude already +4.3% off Wednesday's low.
